When both candidates are re-scored at every comparison, as in the minibatch acceptance gates of prompt optimizers, keep-if-better is a reversible Markov chain if the score difference is logistic and the mutation operator is reversible, and its stationary law is the mutation equilibrium tilted by exp(beta f). For any continuous symmetric noise difference the same tilt is the stationary law of a small-step diffusion limit, with beta = 4F'(0); for a minibatch gate beta grows with the square root of the minibatch size. Caching the incumbent's score instead inflates the recorded score. We test the tilt as a prediction for LLM-guided program search, committing each prediction from calibration data before the search runs. The level after 150 steps rises with the minibatch size in six of seven settings, but its predicted value fails: on bin packing, search attains 62-88% of the predicted gain when the proposer edits the parent and 109-119% when it writes new heuristics. The attained fraction falls with the parent-child quality correlation of unselected mutation; a registered test on two new settings confirmed the direction, but not the quantitative agreement after a correction. Further registered tests found that runs started from a good program kept losing quality over 300 steps, more so from starts that search had selected, by a margin that passed its registered rule narrowly. Runs from different starts had not reached a common level, so whether the tilt describes the stationary law of LLM editing remains open. A registered test in prompt optimisation on frozen task-model scores failed: search exceeded the tilt, and the bin-packing relation did not transfer.
Machine Learning.comment: 34 pages, 5 figures. Pre-registered predictions, code and data checksums are described in Appendix C

Machine Learning.title: Closed-Form Last Layer Optimization
Machine Learning.summary: Neural networks are typically optimized with variants of stochastic gradient descent. Under a squared loss, however, the optimal solution to the linear last layer weights is known in closed-form. We propose to leverage this during optimization, treating the last layer as a function of the backbone parameters, and optimizing solely for these parameters. We show this is equivalent to alternating between gradient descent steps on the backbone and closed-form updates on the last layer. We adapt the method for the setting of stochastic gradient descent, by trading off the loss on the current batch against the accumulated information from previous batches. We provide theoretical analyses showing convergence of the method to an optimal solution in the neural tangent kernel regime, as well as quantifying the gains compared to standard SGD in a one-step analysis. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared with SGD and Adam on a squared loss in several regression tasks, including neural operators and causal inference.

Machine Learning.title: Automatic feature identification in least-squares policy iteration using the Koopman operator framework
Machine Learning.summary: In this paper, we present a Koopman autoencoder-based least-squares policy iteration (KAE-LSPI) algorithm for reinforcement learning (RL). The KAE-LSPI algorithm is based on reformulating the so-called least-squares fixed-point approximation method in terms of extended dynamic mode decomposition (EDMD), thereby enabling automatic feature learning via the Koopman autoencoder (KAE) framework. The approach is motivated by the lack of a systematic procedure for selecting features or kernels in linear RL techniques. Unlike previous approaches, no features or kernels need to be fixed a priori in our method. We discuss the theoretical convergence of KAE-LSPI under suitable assumptions, similar to kernel-based least-squares policy iteration (KLSPI). We empirically compare our method with two existing algorithms: least-squares policy iteration (LSPI) and KLSPI. In particular, for the chainwalk problem, the resulting policies are either optimal or nearly optimal for both three approaches. For the cart-pole system, KAE-LSPI outperforms the other two approaches in terms of policy performance.
Machine Learning.comment: 15 pages, 4 figures

Machine Learning.title: Flow-Direct: Feedback-Efficient and Reusable Guidance for Flow Models via Non-Parametric Guidance Field
Machine Learning.summary: Training-free guidance enables pre-trained diffusion and flow models to optimize application-specific objectives using feedback from external black-box reward functions. However, existing methods are feedback-inefficient because reward feedback is used only transiently to inform a localized gradient approximation or a discrete search decision, and is subsequently discarded. To address this limitation, we propose Flow-Direct, a framework that guides the generation process via a persistent guidance field. Theoretically, this guidance field is analytically derived from the log-density ratio between the base and reward-weighted target distributions; it transports the pre-trained distribution to the target distribution. In practice, the field is implemented as a non-parametric estimator constructed from all accumulated reward-evaluated samples. As more samples are collected during optimization, this empirical guidance field becomes increasingly accurate. This persistent formulation yields two major advantages. First, Flow-Direct is highly feedback-efficient: because every evaluated sample is used to refine the global guidance field, no reward information is wasted. Second, the framework is naturally reusable: once optimization is complete, the collected dataset defines a reusable guidance field for generating novel target samples without additional reward evaluations, and distinct guidance fields can be combined to generate samples that simultaneously satisfy multiple objectives.

stat Machine Learning.title: Support Vector Machines Directly Minimise KL Divergence
stat Machine Learning.summary: Support vector machines (SVMs) are fundamentally grounded in geometric margin maximisation and currently lack a mainstream probabilistic interpretation. This keeps them theoretically isolated from probabilistic machine learning models that are naturally comparable and combinable. In this paper, we bridge this gap by proving that the dual objectives of both support vector classification and support vector regression are exact, constrained Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence minimisation tasks between two Gaussian measures. We further show that this same divergence formulation recovers the exact objective function for kernel ridge regression when domain constraints are removed and $L^2$ regularisation is applied. By demonstrating that SVM duals directly minimise relative entropy, our results provide a unified information-theoretic model for standard kernel machines and lay the foundation for unifying broader kernel-based algorithms under probability theory.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 14 pages, 1 table, v2 includes section on optimal solution

stat Machine Learning.title: Quasipolynomial-Time Planning for Decodable POMDPs
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study planning for finite-horizon partially observable Markov decision processes (POMDPs) with finite state, action, and observation spaces. Both exact and approximate planning are known to be computationally hard in this setting, so prior work has explored natural assumptions that make planning easier. Recent work [Golowich et al., 2022] gave quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for observable POMDPs. These are POMDPs whose observation channels satisfy an $\ell_1$-observability condition, but notably, no assumptions are required on the transition dynamics. In a similar vein, for every fixed $ρ>0$, we give quasipolynomial-time approximate planning algorithms for $ρ$-decodable POMDPs. We show that decodability is implied by both $\ell_1$- and $\ell_2$-observability and is strictly weaker than observability. Moreover, we show that the optimal decodability constant can be computed in polynomial time, whereas computing the optimal $\ell_1$-observability constant is NP-hard in the worst case. We also show that the fast filter-forgetting guarantee underlying the approach of [Golowich et al., 2022] does not extend directly from $\ell_1$-observability to constant $\ell_2$-observability. Thus, decodability is an easy-to-check, unifying assumption under which quasipolynomial-time approximate planning for POMDPs is possible.

stat Machine Learning.title: Instance-Optimal Estimation with Multiple LLM Judges on a Budget
stat Machine Learning.summary: Evaluating large language models increasingly relies on LLM-as-a-judge protocols, but such evaluations remain costly: different judges have different prices and reliabilities, and the difficulty of each prompt-response pair can vary substantially. This raises a basic allocation question: under a fixed budget, how should one distribute evaluation queries across heterogeneous judges and instances to obtain the most accurate score estimates? We formalize this question as budgeted heteroskedastic multi-judge estimation under independent, unbiased score observations. Given $K$ prompt-response pairs and $J$ judges with known costs but unknown query-judge variances, our goal is to estimate the bounded score vector while minimizing an $\ell_p$-error. Our first contribution is to analyze the inverse-variance weighted estimator (IVWE) and to derive the oracle allocation that minimizes its leading error bound. Since this allocation depends on the unknown variances, we then address the unknown-variance setting by proposing EST-IVWE, an adaptive algorithm that constructs and uses optimistic variance estimates to stabilize the empirical allocation. We prove that EST-IVWE matches the oracle IVWE rate up to lower-order terms in the budget. Our second and central theoretical contribution is a local minimax lower bound matching the leading allocation-dependent rate, establishing asymptotic instance-optimality up to logarithmic factors. An Assouad-type construction based on local, variance-preserving perturbations yields this bound both in expectation and with constant probability. A complementary Fano-type change-of-measure argument captures the logarithmic dependence on the confidence level with a different (suboptimal) allocation geometry. Finally, we numerically validate our approach on synthetic data and resampled HelpSteer2 evaluations, demonstrating improvements over naïve uniform allocation.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 55 pages, 4 figures; the first two authors contributed equally

stat Machine Learning.summary: Language-model systems can select prompts and parameter adapters repeatedly during deployment, using feedback to guide later choices. stat Machine Learning.title: A Generalized Bayesian Approach to Clustering with Dimension Reduction
stat Machine Learning.summary: Generalized Bayes product partition models provide a probabilistic counterpart to loss-based clustering. They update a prior over partitions through an exponentiated clustering loss rather than a likelihood, so allocation uncertainty can be quantified without a full generative model for the data. However, their performance depends on the space in which the loss is evaluated. For high-dimensional observations, a squared Euclidean loss on the raw features can be dominated by irrelevant coordinates or fail to reflect cluster structure lying near a nonlinear low-dimensional manifold. We propose an extension in which an autoencoder and the partition are learned together, so that the space in which the clustering loss is evaluated is shaped by the clustering itself. Our generalized posterior combines a reconstruction loss, which keeps the low-dimensional representation faithful to the observed data, with a within-cluster sum of squares in the latent representation, which encourages cluster separation. Posterior computation alternates between Gibbs sampling over partitions and gradient-based updates of the autoencoder network, with the learning rate estimated jointly. We illustrate the approach through simulation studies and applications to four benchmark datasets.

stat Machine Learning.title: Closed-Form Last Layer Optimization
stat Machine Learning.summary: Neural networks are typically optimized with variants of stochastic gradient descent. Under a squared loss, however, the optimal solution to the linear last layer weights is known in closed-form. We propose to leverage this during optimization, treating the last layer as a function of the backbone parameters, and optimizing solely for these parameters. We show this is equivalent to alternating between gradient descent steps on the backbone and closed-form updates on the last layer. We adapt the method for the setting of stochastic gradient descent, by trading off the loss on the current batch against the accumulated information from previous batches. We provide theoretical analyses showing convergence of the method to an optimal solution in the neural tangent kernel regime, as well as quantifying the gains compared to standard SGD in a one-step analysis. Finally, we demonstrate the effectiveness of our approach compared with SGD and Adam on a squared loss in several regression tasks, including neural operators and causal inference.

stat Machine Learning.title: Optimizing Computational-Statistical Runtime for Wasserstein Distance Estimation
stat Machine Learning.summary: Squared Wasserstein distance is a frequently used tool to measure discrepancy between probability distributions. This distance is typically computed between empirical measures of size $n$ from two underlying random samples. Unfortunately, even in lower dimensional Euclidean space problems $\left( d \in \{2,3\} \right)$, algorithms for Wasserstein distance computation with approximate or exact precision guarantees scale poorly in the runtime as a function of $n$ and the desired precision. In response, we consider the computational-statistical runtime, where the goal is to estimate from samples the Wasserstein distance between potentially smooth measures up to $ε$-additive error in expectation with respect to the sampling; we allow $O(1)$ computational cost for collecting a sample. Towards this, we develop a Sample-Sketch-Solve paradigm where we introduce a regular cartesian grid sketch of the samples. We show that (especially under $α$-Hölder smooth distributions) this can compress the data without increasing asymptotic error, and also regularizes the structure which enables faster exact algorithms. Ultimately, we approximate $W_2^2(P,Q)$ within $ε$ error in $ε^{-\max(2,\frac{d+1+o(1)}{1+α})}$ time for $0 < α< 1$ Hölder smooth distributions $P,Q$ on $(0,1)^{d}$; an optimal $Θ(ε^{-2})$ for $α> 1/2$ when $d=2$ and nearly optimal as $α\to 1$ when $d = 3$.

stat Machine Learning.title: Online Causal Configuration for Networked Systems via Doubly Robust Steady-State Learning
stat Machine Learning.summary: Measurement exploration reveals how interacting local controllers behave but can alter the steady-state regime a network operator seeks to optimize. Exploratory rewards may therefore fail to identify a configuration's no-exploration value: under full exploration, identical logged distributions can conceal different target values. Identification requires accounting for both action-law mismatch and shifts in the steady-state context distribution. We introduce CAUSAL-UCB, which selects configurations using optimistic bounds on target causal values. Its interference-aware clipped doubly robust evaluator produces predecision certificates separating statistical variation from calibrated identification, transport, and temporal-dependence errors. For any finite horizon and predetermined schedule of measurement-exploration rates $\{η_t\}$, we prove lower bounds of $Ω((1+\sum_tη_t)^{-1/2})$ on minimax inference error and $Ω(\sum_tη_t)$ on measurement-induced deployment loss in a stationary, potentially slow-mixing family. We bound regret under valid certificates and selected-information growth, and establish an anytime finite-sample certificate with a shared radius for estimation, selection, and reporting in a restricted known-local-interference model. In a high-mismatch benchmark with 24 paired seeds and 200 rounds, CAUSAL-UCB attains target regret of $1.732$ versus $6.326$ for certified IPS-UCB, with deployment gaps of $30.607$ and $23.217$, respectively. Independent-audit coverage tests and trace-driven semi-synthetic studies further assess certificate coverage and deployment trade-offs.

stat Machine Learning.title: Outlier-Robust Multi-Output Gaussian Processes
stat Machine Learning.summary: Multi-output Gaussian process (MOGP) regression allows modelling dependencies among multiple correlated response variables. Similarly to standard Gaussian processes (GPs), MOGPs are sensitive to model misspecification and outliers, which can distort predictions within individual outputs. In the multi-output case, this situation can be further exacerbated as anomalous observations in one response can adversely influence predictions for other correlated outputs. To handle this situation, we propose R-MOGP, an MOGP that is provably robust to outliers in any individual response. Our approach preserves conjugacy, achieving robustness without sacrificing computational efficiency, and integrates naturally with sparse variational inference for scalability. Empirically, we show that R-MOGP achieves performance comparable to existing state-of-the-art robust MOGPs at a fraction of their computational costs.

stat Machine Learning.title: Kernel-Based Learning of Analytic Operators and Parametric PDEs
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study kernel-based learning of analytic operators from finite samples, with a focus on how the regularity of the target should determine the choice of the kernel. We establish embeddings of analytic operators into vector-valued reproducing kernel Hilbert spaces and derive finite-sample, high-probability guarantees that quantify the uncertainty due to random sampling: in the noiseless setting, suitable analytic kernels yield rates exponential in a fractional power of the sample size, while Sobolev-type kernels yield polynomial rates. We apply the theory to the solution operator of a parametric elliptic PDE, where the training data are themselves finite-element approximations, and obtain bounds that separate the sampling and discretization contributions to the error and prescribe how the mesh size should be coupled to the sample size. The results are illustrated numerically.

stat Machine Learning.title: Linear Bandits on Ellipsoids: Minimax Optimal Algorithms
stat Machine Learning.summary: We consider linear stochastic bandits where the set of actions is an ellipsoid. We provide the first known minimax optimal algorithm for this problem. We first derive a novel information-theoretic lower bound on the regret of any algorithm, which must be at least $Ω(\min(d σ\sqrt{T} + d \|θ\|_{A}, \|θ\|_{A} T))$ where $d$ is the dimension, $T$ the time horizon, $σ^2$ the noise variance, $A$ a matrix defining the set of actions and $θ$ the vector of unknown parameters. We then provide an algorithm whose regret matches this bound to a multiplicative universal constant. The algorithm is non-classical in the sense that it is not optimistic, and it is not a sampling algorithm. The main idea is to combine a novel sequential procedure to estimate $\|θ\|$, followed by an explore-and-commit strategy informed by this estimate. The algorithm is highly computationally efficient, and a run requires only time $O(dT + d^2 \log(T/d) + d^3)$ and memory $O(d^2)$, in contrast with known optimistic algorithms, which are not implementable in polynomial time. We go beyond minimax optimality and show that our algorithm is locally asymptotically minimax optimal, a much stronger notion of optimality. We further provide numerical experiments to illustrate our theoretical findings.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 21 pages, 3 figures; fix a typo in the COLT 2025 published version regarding the lower bound parametrization of alternatives

stat Machine Learning.title: Spectrum-Adaptive Generalization Bounds for Trained Deep Transformers
stat Machine Learning.summary: Understanding why trained Transformers generalize well is a fundamental problem in modern machine learning theory, and complexity-based generalization bounds provide a principled way to study this question. While existing norm-based bounds for Transformers remove the explicit polynomial dependence on the hidden dimension, they typically impose fixed norm constraints specified a priori and can exhibit unfavorable exponential dependence on depth. In this paper, we derive spectrum-adaptive post hoc generalization bounds for multi-layer Transformers. Under layerwise spectral norm control, the bounds are expressed in terms of layerwise Schatten quantities of the query-key, value, and feedforward weight matrices. Since the Schatten indices need not be fixed a priori and can instead be selected after training, separately for each matrix type and layer, the bounds adaptively trade off spectral complexity against the dimension- and depth-dependent factors according to the learned singular-value profiles. Empirical comparisons of BERT-adapted proxies for the leading complexity factors suggest that the proxies induced by our bounds grow more slowly with depth and hidden dimension than the corresponding norm-based proxies. Overall, our results provide a complexity-based perspective on how the spectral structure of trained Transformers is reflected in generalization analyses.

stat Machine Learning.title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
stat Machine Learning.summary: This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions. Therein, the non-conformity scores are normalized with an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on the log-transformed leave-one-out residuals of the base model. We show that the coverage guarantee of jackknife+ conformal prediction carries over to the adaptive intervals if the leave-one-out auxiliary models are trained on nested leave-one-out residuals. For fixed-basis polynomial chaos expansions fitted by ordinary least squares, all required quantities are derived in closed form and the guarantee-preserving adaptive intervals are obtained from a single model fit, without any model retraining. For sparse polynomial chaos expansions, where multiple model fits are necessary, we propose a heuristic simplification that limits the computational overhead of adaptivity at the cost of the formal coverage guarantee. Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset show that the suggested method attains the target coverage while providing intervals that adapt to local prediction uncertainty, therefore being considerably more statistically efficient. These advantages are particularly prominent in high-uncertainty regions of the input space, where the performance of non-adaptive methods degrades substantially.

stat Machine Learning.title: Marginal-Nonuniform Multiclass Learning
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study the problem of multiclass classification within the framework of marginal-nonuniform learning, where the constants in the learning rate may depend on the unknown marginal distribution generating the unlabeled data, but not on the target concept. This notion naturally lies between classical PAC learning, where the constants are independent of both the marginal distribution and the target concept, and more recent universal learning, where the constants may depend on both. We give a complete characterization of the optimal marginal-nonuniform learning rates, establishing a fundamental trichotomy: exponential, linear, and arbitrarily slow rates. This characterization is witnessed by a new combinatorial dimension, termed the uncentered DS-eluder dimension. A key ingredient in the upper-bound proofs is a set of new distributional exhaustion lemmas that exploit the sequential nature of this dimension and may be of independent interest.

stat Machine Learning.title: Smooth Piecewise Cutting for Neural Operator to Handle Discontinuities and Sharp Transitions
stat Machine Learning.summary: Neural operators have achieved strong performance in learning solution operators of partial differential equations (PDEs), but their inherently continuous representations struggle to capture discontinuities and sharp transitions. Existing approaches typically approximate such features within continuous function spaces, often requiring increased model capacity and high-resolution data. In this work, we propose Cut-DeepONet, a two-stage training framework that explicitly models discontinuities while reducing learning complexity. Our approach reformulates the problem via a lifting strategy, partitioning the domain into smooth subregions while representing discontinuities as boundaries in a higher-dimensional space. This separation aligns the operator learning task with the inductive bias of neural networks and avoids directly approximating discontinuities. An additional network predicts input-dependent discontinuity locations for unseen inputs, which are then used to guide the neural operator in generating smooth components within each region. Experiments on benchmark PDEs show that Cut-DeepONet outperforms state-of-the-art methods, even when trained on low-resolution datasets. The method excels on problems with discontinuities and sharp transitions, while using fewer trainable parameters. Our results highlight the benefits of changing the representation of operator learning rather than increasing model complexity.

stat Machine Learning.title: Matrix Factorization Framework for Community Detection under the Degree-Corrected Block Model
stat Machine Learning.summary: Community detection is a fundamental task in data analysis, and block models provide an approach for identifying diverse community structures. The degree-corrected block model (DCBM) is an established model that captures node degree heterogeneity. However, inference methods are computationally costly and sensitive to initialization, while cheaper alternatives, such as spectral or modularity-based approaches, may be less effective at recovering certain non-assortative structures. In this work, we show that DCBM inference can be reformulated as a constrained nonnegative matrix trifactorization problem. Leveraging this insight, we propose a scalable community detection method with a theoretically grounded initialization providing an initial partition for inference algorithms. Our approach is agnostic to network structure and applies to any graph representable by a DCBM. Experiments on synthetic and real-world benchmark networks show that our method achieves community recovery comparable to, and sometimes better than, that achieved by the DCBM inference methods, while being faster: it processes a graph with 100,000 nodes and 500,000 edges in about 30 seconds. Moreover, the initialization significantly improves solution quality. Overall, this work provides a scalable and robust framework for community detection and highlights the benefits of a matrix-factorization perspective for the DCBM.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 19 pages, 7 figures, code and data available from https://github.com/Alexia1305/OtrisymNMF_DCBM

stat Machine Learning.title: Optimal In-context Adaptivity and Distributional Robustness of Transformers
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study in-context learning problems where a Transformer is pretrained on tasks drawn from a mixture distribution $π=\sum_{α\in\mathcal{A}} λ_α π_α$, called the pretraining prior, in which each mixture component $π_α$ is a distribution on tasks of a specific difficulty level indexed by $α$. Our goal is to understand the performance of the pretrained Transformer when evaluated on a different test distribution $μ$, consisting of tasks of fixed difficulty $β\in\mathcal{A}$, and with potential distribution shift relative to $π_β$, subject to the chi-squared divergence $χ^2(μ,π_β)$ being at most $κ$. In particular, we consider nonparametric regression problems with random smoothness, and multi-index models with both random smoothness and random effective dimension. We prove that a large Transformer pretrained on sufficient data achieves the optimal rate of convergence corresponding to the difficulty level $β$, uniformly over test distributions $μ$ in the chi-squared divergence ball. Thus, the pretrained Transformer is able to achieve faster rates of convergence on easier tasks and is robust to distribution shift at test time. Finally, we prove that even if an estimator had access to the test distribution $μ$, the convergence rate of its expected risk over $μ$ could not be faster than that of our pretrained Transformers, thereby providing a more appropriate optimality guarantee than minimax lower bounds.

stat Machine Learning.title: Training-Free Generative Sampling via Moment-Matched Score Smoothing
stat Machine Learning.summary: Diffusion models generate samples by denoising along the score of a perturbed target distribution. In practice, one trains a neural diffusion model, which is computationally expensive. Recent work suggests that score matching implicitly smooths the empirical score, and that this smoothing bias promotes generalization by capturing low-dimensional data geometry. We propose moment-matched score-smoothed overdamped Langevin dynamics (MM-SOLD), a training-free interacting particle sampler that enforces the target moments throughout the sampling trajectory. We prove that the one-particle marginal of the ideal constrained Gibbs equilibrium converges, as the number of particles grows, to a Gibbs--Boltzmann density obtained by exponentially tilting the naive score-smoothed target. Its mean and covariance match the training GMM, even for rank-deficient data. We additionally establish sampling consistency, statistical target-error bounds for bounded data, and consistency of a safeguarded BAOAB-based tilting estimator. Experiments on 2D distributions and latent-space image generation show that MM-SOLD enables fast, robust, latent sampling on CPUs using fixed pretrained autoencoders, with sample fidelity and diversity competitive with neural diffusion baselines.

stat Machine Learning.title: k-Volume: a Unified Active Learning Strategy
stat Machine Learning.summary: In the classification context where revealing the label of a sample is costly, we propose a new Active Learning (AL) strategy named k-Volume (kVol). It randomly selects a sample to be labeled according to the volume of the smallest ball containing its k nearest neighbors. kVol is highly versatile: it can be applied either in the input space or in the output space, and it enjoys the desirable properties of the three main families of AL strategies: density, diversity, and (when performed in the output space) uncertainty. From a theoretical perspective, we establish that kVol is asymptotically equivalent to uniform sampling over the support of the (input or output) data distribution. Based on experiments on various synthetic and real-life tabular datasets and images, we observe that kVol is surprisingly stable: whatever the classifier or the experimental setup, it still lies among the best AL strategies unlike other competitors that fail dramatically. In particular, kVol outperforms state-of-the-art competitors such as CoreSet, TypiClust or Uncertainty on several real-life datasets, at a low computational cost.

stat Machine Learning.title: Action-BED: Task-Driven Bayesian Experimental Design with Singly Intractable Objectives
stat Machine Learning.summary: Bayesian experimental design (BED) has traditionally been based on maximising expected uncertainty reductions from prior to posterior. A major shortfall of this approach is that it leads to doubly intractable objectives that are difficult to optimise, while customising them to particular downstream tasks of interest can also be difficult. Following first principles decision theory, we demonstrate that BED can alternatively be formulated in terms of an expected future loss (EFL) on downstream actions, providing a simple and naturally task-driven framework. Critically, we then show that all such EFLs can be rearranged into singly intractable objectives that can be jointly optimised with respect to both the design policy and a downstream action policy using stochastic gradients, an approach we refer to as ACTION-BED. This formulation further sidesteps the need for any explicit posterior or marginal likelihood estimation and is naturally implicit, requiring only the ability to sample from the joint model over model parameters and data, and evaluate the downstream loss function. It thus allows design policies to be learned more effectively, efficiently, and simply than existing methods, while providing easy customisation to different downstream tasks and losses.
stat Machine Learning.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. Camera-ready version; revised presentation, additional experiments, and corrected references

stat Machine Learning.title: Closed-form fractional radial links for elliptical Mahalanobis discriminant analysis
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study binary classification when the two classes are elliptical with a shared radial generator $g$. The log-likelihood ratio is then an additive function of the two squared Mahalanobis radii, with radial link $\varphi=\log g$. For Gaussian classes $\varphi$ is affine and the rule reduces to quadratic discriminant analysis (QDA); otherwise the Bayes link is not the identity. Instead of fitting this link with a spline smoother, we derive its family from the within-class law of the radius and estimate a finite fractional-power projection. We prove that the link is identifiable from the radius law, that the plug-in estimator is $\sqrt{n}$-consistent and asymptotically normal under finite-moment conditions, and that the induced classifier is asymptotically Bayes-optimal in an iterated sieve limit. For $d\ge2$ and non-nested class parameters, the identity link suffices only for affine (Gaussian) generators. The bridge, GAM membership and the affine direction of this dichotomy are verified in Lean 4. We compare against the global Mahalanobis-GAM of Ghosh et al. (2025), re-implemented with mgcv REML splines at equal input budget. On two UCI benchmarks the derived link ties with the fitted GAM. On six financial series from three asset classes, with validation that respects temporal dependence, it is never significantly worse than the fitted GAM: better on CAD/USD and tied on the other five. It beats QDA on the three heaviest-tailed series (oil $[+0.023,+0.069]$, S&P 500 $[+0.039,+0.125]$, JPY/USD $[+0.009,+0.047]$) and ties elsewhere. A rate simulation with a closed-form ground truth reproduces the $\sqrt{n}$ rate and, under covariance heterogeneity, QDA's risk floor against the derived link's vanishing excess risk. The derived link thus matches a tuned GAM without smoothing-parameter selection and improves on QDA where the generator departs from the Gaussian.

stat Machine Learning.title: Ensemble Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimisation
stat Machine Learning.summary: We study zeroth-order optimisation under context distributional uncertainty, a setting commonly tackled using Bayesian optimisation (BO). A prevailing strategy to make BO more robust to the complex and noisy nature of data is to employ an ensemble as the surrogate model, thereby mitigating the weaknesses of any single model. In this study, we propose a novel algorithm for Ensemble Distributionally Robust Bayesian Optimisation that remains computationally tractable while managing continuous context. We obtain theoretical sublinear regret bounds, improving current state-of-the-art results. We show that our method's empirical behaviour aligns with its theoretical guarantees.

stat Machine Learning.title: Conformal Prediction for Time-Dependent PDEs
stat Machine Learning.summary: Uncertainty quantification is crucial in scientific machine learning, where models inform safety-critical tasks such as flood forecasting, financial risk management, and thermal control in machines. Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees, but in time-dependent settings common to physics and engineering, these guarantees can break down, leading to systematic undercoverage. We study this problem in the context of surrogate models for time-dependent physical systems described by partial differential equations. We prove that in a function space setting, distributions at arbitrarily close times can be mutually singular, making exact coverage guarantees impossible. We further show that in discretized settings, the total variation distance between distributions often saturates exponentially fast with the grid resolution, mandating restrictions on the spatial discretization to ensure coverage. Finally, for certain settings, we show how to use principled weighted conformal prediction to obtain finite-sample coverage guarantees over growing time horizons.

stat Machine Learning.title: CausalCompass: Evaluating the Robustness of Time-Series Causal Discovery in Misspecified Scenarios
stat Machine Learning.summary: Causal discovery from time series is a fundamental task in machine learning. However, its widespread adoption is hindered by a reliance on untestable causal assumptions and by the lack of robustness-oriented evaluation in existing benchmarks. To address these challenges, we propose CausalCompass, a flexible and extensible benchmark framework designed to assess the robustness of time-series causal discovery (TSCD) methods under violations of modeling assumptions. To demonstrate the practical utility of CausalCompass, we conduct extensive benchmarking of representative TSCD algorithms across eight assumption-violation scenarios. Our experimental results indicate that no single method consistently attains optimal performance across all settings. Nevertheless, in most scenarios, the methods exhibiting superior overall performance are deep learning-based approaches. We further provide hyperparameter sensitivity analyses to deepen the understanding of these findings. We additionally conduct ablation experiments to explain the strong performance of deep learning-based methods under assumption violations. We also find that NTS-NOTEARS relies on standardized preprocessing in practice, performing poorly in the vanilla setting but exhibiting strong performance after standardization. Finally, our work aims to provide a comprehensive and systematic evaluation of TSCD methods under assumption violations, thereby facilitating their broader adoption in real-world applications. The user-friendly implementation, documentation and datasets are available at https://github.com/huiyang-yi/CausalCompass.

stat Machine Learning.title: Hypergraph Generation via Structured Stochastic Diffusion
stat Machine Learning.summary: Hypergraphs model higher-order interactions, but realistic hypergraph generation remains difficult because incidence, hyperedge-size heterogeneity, and overlap structure are not faithfully captured by pairwise reductions. We propose \HEDGE, a generative model defined directly on relaxed incidence matrices via a structured stochastic diffusion. The forward process combines a hypergraph-specific two-sided heat operator with an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck component, preserving structure-aware noising near the data while yielding an explicit Gaussian terminal law. Conditional on an observed hypergraph, this forward process is linear-Gaussian, so conditional means, covariances, scores, and reverse-drift targets are available in closed form. We therefore learn a permutation-equivariant state-only reverse-drift field in incidence space by regressing onto exact conditional targets, and generate samples by simulating a learned reverse-time SDE from the Gaussian base law. We establish exactness in the ideal state-only setting together with finite-horizon stability guarantees, and empirically show improved hypergraph generation quality relative to strong baselines.

stat Machine Learning.title: Measuring and Decomposing Mode Separation via the Canonical Diffusion
stat Machine Learning.summary: Mode separation, namely how sharply a distribution fragments into barrier-separated clusters, is a fundamental geometric property of densities, difficult to quantify in high dimensions. Modes are often the meaningful alternatives in the data, such as the conformations of a molecule or the distinct semantic types among a generative model's outputs. Mode separation is distinct from dispersion, which is what standard label-free tools capture: differential entropy rises with spread regardless of fragmentation, and PCA orders directions by variance regardless of barriers. Mutual information does capture it, but only given the latent component labels, which are usually unavailable. We measure mode separation through a single stochastic process intrinsic to the density, namely the unique reversible diffusion with $f$ as its stationary distribution and a constant scalar diffusion coefficient. From its autocovariance matrix we extract two readouts. The first, SSA (Sum of Squared Autocorrelations), is a scalar barrier-sensitive measure. The second, DA (Dominant Autocorrelation directions), gives linear projections ordered by metastability rather than variance. Under an isotropic-Gaussian null, we derive the limiting spectrum of the empirical autocovariance in closed form, generalizing the Marchenko--Pastur law. Its upper edge gives a noise floor that separates metastable directions from sampling noise. Both readouts use only samples and a score function, scaling to high dimensions through pretrained score-based generative models via Tweedie's identity. We apply our framework to three settings: (i) synthetic Gaussian mixtures, where SSA tracks mutual information; (ii) SDXL text-to-image generations, where SSA and DA capture structure that entropy and PCA miss; and (iii) molecular dynamics of alanine dipeptide, where DA recovers the known slow backbone dihedrals from static samples alone.

stat Machine Learning.title: Calibrating your confidence requires thinking of all the ways you could be wrong
stat Machine Learning.summary:
A primary limitation of modern deep learning is the miscalibration of model confidence; traditional architectures fundamentally lack a mechanism to quantify their own uncertainty. Larger models and larger datasets mitigate this issue, but they do not resolve the underlying structural deficiency. Bayesian methods offer a principled uncertainty-aware learning framework through stochastic parameters. Yet, despite the established benefits, the inherent computational overhead often compromises either scalability or quality. This trade-off currently prevents the widespread adoption of Bayesian methods.
  This Thesis bridges the gap between high-quality and low-complexity by introducing a novel distribution on parameter space: a degenerate Gaussian whose covariance is a projection matrix aligned with the null space of the Fisher information matrix. We demonstrate the scalability of this Bayesian posterior through two numerically efficient algorithms: one for posterior sampling and another for the direct computation of predictive confidence. Empirically, we show State-Of-The-Art confidence calibration and out-of-distribution detection for large models.
  We provide theoretical grounding for this approach. We study the degeneracies inherent in Amari's information geometry and highlight its most relevant component: the split of parameter's perturbations into two orthogonal subspaces. From this perspective, our posterior naturally emerges as the simplest choice that captures this split, assigning unitary variance to one subspace and zero variance to the other. Moreover, through the tools of differential geometry, we utilize this split to identify and rectify a critical misalignment issue of the non-linearized Laplace Approximation. Finally, with a focus on PAC-Bayes generalization bounds, we pave the way for a deeper understanding of the learning capabilities of overparametrized models.
stat Machine Learning.comment: PhD Thesis, Technical University of Denmark (DTU), 2026

stat Machine Learning.title: Enforcing Symmetries on Pre-trained ML Models for Physics
stat Machine Learning.summary: Post-hoc group averaging (or test-time augmentation) is a simple way to impose symmetry on a trained predictor without changing its architecture or retraining it. For finite and compact groups, averaging over a normalized Haar measure on the group gives the Reynolds operator: a canonical projection onto invariant or equivariant predictors with known non-increasing risk guarantees under certain assumptions. This paper provides numerical experiments on physics emulation models that demonstrate the effectiveness of the approach in this setting. We then extend this framework to non-compact group symmetries. For non-compact groups, the Haar measure cannot be normalized, so group averaging cannot be defined in the same way. We replace it with three alternatives: the Weyl unitary trick (which requires complexifying the space and extending the predictor), a data-dependent orthogonal projection (which involves a non-trivial optimization on the space of invariant or equivariant functions), and a frame averaging approach (which involves mapping each point to a set of orbit representatives). We illustrate the constructions theoretically and empirically on the unit-rescaling group and the Lorentz group. Our results show that in the non-compact case, the Weyl trick and frame averaging do not provide a consistent improvement over the baseline, except where the test data is out-of-distribution (an orders-of-magnitude improvement in this case) and, for the Weyl trick, in low-data regimes. The orthogonal projection can provide improvements in-distribution and out-of-distribution. We also observe that models trained directly on invariant features matched or beat the projection of an unconstrained one. We conclude that post-hoc symmetrization extends to non-compact groups, but it does not consistently outperform training a symmetric model.

stat Machine Learning.title: Fine-Tuned Language Models Exhibit Improved Information Conveyance
stat Machine Learning.summary: Fine-tuning is often believed to reduce uncertainty and diversity in large language models, but existing analyses overlook output length, a key confounder, and therefore fail to capture how uncertainty is distributed across an entire generation rollout. To address this, we propose Canopy Entropy ($\mathrm{CE}^\star$), a measure that views language generation from a tree perspective, where "canopy" represents the space of all possible rollouts, making $\mathrm{CE}^\star$ naturally quantify the effective size of the generation space. $\mathrm{CE}^\star$ jointly captures uncertainty in both the output length $N$ and the generated sequence $Y_{1:N}$ -- indeed, we show that it equals total Shannon entropy $H(N, Y_{1:N}\mid X)$, where $X$ denotes the prompt. This formulation yields interpretable metrics, including a length-entropy correlation term $ρ(N, r_N)$, where $r_N$ is the entropy rate, quantifying information conveyance efficiency by indicating whether longer outputs are more or less informative per token. Empirically, across tasks and model families, we find that fine-tuned models predominantly exhibit more positive correlation $ρ(N, r_N)$, even when total entropy decreases. Furthermore, after controlling for model family, task, prompt, and output-length effects, we find that fine-tuning nearly triples the correlation strength between entropy rate and semantic diversity, suggesting that aligned models convert token uncertainty into semantic diversity more efficiently. Overall, these results demonstrate that fine-tuning does not simply reduce uncertainty, but fundamentally reorganizes it into more informative and semantically meaningful generations. Our code is available at https://github.com/WeiyiTian/canopy-entropy.

stat Machine Learning.title: Ordered Policy Optimization
stat Machine Learning.summary: Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) stabilizes policy updates by clipping the importance ratio between the new policy and the data-collecting policy. The standard rule uses one fixed clipping range for all samples. While this choice offers simplicity and effectiveness, it fails to distinguish statistically harmful extreme ratio values from large, yet tolerable changes. We study how to adapt the clipping radius to the reliability of the induced importance ratio distribution. Our case study demonstrates that reliable updates require controlling these extreme ratios, rather than merely verifying that individual ratios fall within a fixed interval. Motivated by this observation, we propose Ordered Policy Optimization (\textsc{OPO}). In each minibatch, \textsc{OPO} sorts the importance ratios, selects the extreme ratios that potentially have the largest effect on the update, and assigns them adaptive sample-wise radii instead of using the fixed clipping radius. These radii are derived from a prescribed tail profile, which specifies desired target values for the selected extreme ratios. The resulting objective remains first-order and requires only minibatch sorting and a modified policy loss. Experiments conducted on MuJoCo and Atari benchmarks demonstrate that this simple modification achieves strong performance relative to established baselines.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 36 pages, 12 figures, 11 tables. Published in Proc. of the 40th Conference on Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

stat Machine Learning.title: Geometry-Aware Score-Repellent Monte Carlo
stat Machine Learning.summary: The recently proposed Score-Repellent Monte Carlo (SRMC) method improves MCMC sampling by tilting the target density $π$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ with the factor $\exp(-α\,θ_n^\top s(x))$, where the score function $s(x) = \nabla_x \log π(x)$, and $θ_n$ is the score average from past samples. However, a single scalar repellence strength $α\ge0$ cannot handle both the steep and the flat directions in anisotropic energy landscapes at once. We introduce \emph{Geometry-Aware SRMC} (GA-SRMC), which generalizes the Euclidean alignment to $θ^\top M s(x)$ for any symmetric positive-definite matrix $M$. A stochastic-approximation central limit theorem under a trace constraint on $M$ identifies the trace-normalized inverse Fisher $M_{\rm opt}\propto S^{-1}$ as the unique minimizer of the worst-direction covariance bound, elevating the Fisher information $S=\text{Cov}_π(s,s)$ from a proposal-side preconditioner (e.g., FisherMALA, natural gradient) to the bound-optimal repulsion-side matrix, with a single online estimate $\widehat S_n$ serving both roles at no additional computational cost. The full-Fisher online metric $M_n$ converges almost surely to $M_{\rm opt}$ and satisfies a CLT, providing a theoretical guarantee for the online implementation of the GA-SRMC framework. On an $8$-target simulation spanning the condition number $κ\in[1.3,100]$ and dimension $d\in[2,785]$, GA-SRMC dominates SRMC in ESS by $\boldsymbol{4.3\times}$ on anisotropic Gaussian ($κ=100$) and $\boldsymbol{6.8\times}$ on MNIST under the MALA baseline, by $\boldsymbol{16\text{--}32\%}$ on three well-conditioned logistic-regression posteriors, and by up to $\boldsymbol{+48\%}$ under FisherMALA; gains peak on the most anisotropic targets, and posterior-mean MSE is lower than with SRMC in all $16$ full-Fisher implementations.

stat Machine Learning.title: Coreset-Induced Conditional Velocity Flow Matching
stat Machine Learning.summary: We propose Coreset-Induced Conditional Velocity Flow Matching (CCVFM), a generative model that augments hierarchical rectified flow with a data-informed source distribution. Standard flow matching regresses only the conditional mean of the velocity; hierarchical flow matching instead models the full conditional velocity law with a second, inner flow in velocity space, but this inner flow is asked to transport isotropic Gaussian noise to a multimodal target velocity distribution from scratch. Our key observation is that this inner source can be replaced by a closed-form surrogate built from a coreset of the target. CCVFM first compresses the target into weighted atoms using an entropic Sinkhorn coreset and lifts them to a Gaussian mixture. The induced conditional velocity law is then a closed-form Gaussian mixture that can be sampled without a learned neural sampler. A lightweight correction flow, trained from this surrogate source, then refines the remaining surrogate-to-target residual rather than learning an entire noise-to-data map. We prove that the surrogate transport cost equals the target-surrogate Wasserstein gap under an explicit compression assumption, whereas the noise-source analogue has a dimension-scale lower bound. We further characterize the conditional second moment of the training target when the source velocity is drawn from the surrogate law independently of the target velocity, and show that the part of it that depends on the source is small when the surrogate conditional law is close to the true conditional velocity law in mean and covariance. Empirically, on MNIST, CIFAR-10, ImageNet-32, and CelebA-HQ, the proposed method reaches competitive few-step generation under matched architectures. Code is available at https://github.com/ziwaa-se/CCVFM.
stat Machine Learning.comment: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026. 48 pages. Code: https://github.com/ziwaa-se/CCVFM

stat Machine Learning.title: Reweighting for Transfer Classification: Exact Risk Conversion and Minimax Adaptation
stat Machine Learning.summary: A source can make a training mixture easier to learn while making its accuracy less valuable for the target. We study how the training problem a source creates and the finite-sample error of learning it jointly determine target-risk guarantees under reweighting. For binary classification, for each pair of laws and each positive target weight, we derive the sharpest target excess hinge-risk bound implied by mixture excess alone, uniformly over clipped predictors. This exact conversion curve is determined by density-weighted local votes. A two-sample oracle inequality for weighted support vector machines supplies the mixture excess, and the composition becomes explicit for Gaussian kernels. On a tilted-boundary class, we establish the all-procedure minimax classification rate $[n+s_+^2/(m^{-1}+τ^2)]^{-1}$ in the transferable strength $s_+$ and the tilt $τ$, separating source sampling uncertainty ($m^{-1}$) from relation uncertainty ($τ^2$). A target-checked Gaussian-SVM selector adapts to unknown $s_+$ and $τ$ up to a logarithmic factor for fixed dimension, and retains the target-only rate up to the same factor against arbitrary independent sources under the stated target model. On a separate smooth opposition class, the minimax risk within the family of exact Gaussian SVMs fitted to the original labels with nonnegative weights is exponentially larger than the unrestricted minimax risk whenever the target sample is at most half the source sample, despite arbitrary data-dependent weighting and tuning. The value of a source thus depends on the training problem it creates, on what accuracy there means for the target, and on whether the permitted use of the source can implement the needed correction.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 87 pages, 5 figures. Main text (32 pages) followed by the Supplementary Material

stat Machine Learning.title: Guidance for Prior Change via Density Ratio Estimation
stat Machine Learning.summary: Simulation-Based Inference (SBI) serves as a vital framework for parameter inference in scientific fields where simulators involve intractable likelihoods, yet while amortized generative models offer rapid posterior estimation, they are often restricted by the specific priors used during training, thereby limiting their flexibility as prior knowledge evolves. To address this prior dependency, PriorGuide was introduced as an inference-time guidance method, but due to its intractable formulation, it relies on Gaussian approximations of the reverse transition kernel and Gaussian mixture model fitting for the prior ratio, both of which introduce systematic bias. Motivated by these limitations, we propose an unbiased test-time guidance framework that leverages Density Ratio Estimation (DRE) to learn a score guidance term, effectively decoupling the inference process from the prior training. Moreover, our framework remains agnostic to the specific density ratio estimators, making it a general and flexible framework for handling prior changes. Experimental results across multiple tasks demonstrate that our method matches or outperforms PriorGuide on C2ST and MMD in most tasks while maintaining robustness even under limited overlap between the training and target priors. Furthermore, we apply our method to Bayesian updating for parameter inference from planetary light-curve data, where it also demonstrates strong effectiveness and robustness. Code is available at https://github.com/a-chenchen/dre-based-prior-guidance .

stat Machine Learning.title: Model-Agnostic FDR Control via Group Gaussian Mirror and Permutation SHAP
stat Machine Learning.summary: Most FDR-controlled feature selection methods are designed for coordinate-wise hypotheses, where each feature has a single weight or importance score. This abstraction fails in sequential and grouped models, where one original feature is represented by a block of sub-features, such as lags, recurrent states, or attention-based interactions. We propose a grouped-feature FDR control framework for such settings. For grouped linear models, we construct null-symmetric block-level mirror statistics with matrix-valued perturbations. For neural sequential models, we combine Permutation SHAP derivatives as model-agnostic block-level importance scores with kernel-based dependence measure. The framework is model-agnostic across network architectures, does not require specifying the covariate distribution, and reduces to Gaussian Mirror or Neural Gaussian Mirror when the block size is one. We prove FDR control for low- and high-dimensional grouped linear models and asymptotic symmetry of smoothed Permutation SHAP derivatives under fixed fitted nonlinear models. Experiments on simulated and real-world datasets show reliable FDR control and improved power under correlated grouped-feature signals.

stat Machine Learning.title: Sparse Network Inference under Imperfect Detection and its Application to Ecological Networks
stat Machine Learning.summary: Recovering latent structure from count data has received considerable attention in network inference, particularly when one seeks both cross-group interactions and within-group similarity patterns in bipartite networks, which are widely used in ecology research. Such networks are often sparse and prone to imperfect detection. Existing models mainly focus on interaction recovery, while the induced similarity graphs are much less studied. Moreover, existing models for under-counted data place sparsity, if at all, on the detection model rather than on these graphs. To address these issues, we propose a nonnegative low-rank factorization framework that jointly estimates detection probabilities and promotes sparse within- and cross-group graphs through $\ell_{1/2}$ regularization. For the resulting nonconvex, nonsmooth problem, we develop an ADMM-based algorithm with adaptive penalization, and establish asymptotic feasibility and KKT stationarity of cluster points under stated assumptions. We also give sufficient conditions for exact recovery of within- and cross-group graphs. On synthetic data with up to 20% missing entries, the method recovers the graphs and detection probabilities with competitive accuracy. Across three ecological datasets, it matches the baseline held-out predictions while estimating detection probabilities and within- and cross-group graphs.

stat Machine Learning.title: Beyond the Lower-Star Filtration: Alternative Filtration Methods for Persistent Homology
stat Machine Learning.summary: In the lower-star filtration (LSF), simplices are assigned filtration values according to the maximum-vertex rule, with each simplex entering the filtration when its highest-valued vertex appears. A limitation of this construction is that some higher-dimensional simplices may enter simultaneously with their boundary faces, causing certain topological features to be filled immediately upon formation and thus not appear in the resulting persistence diagram. To address this limitation, we propose three alternative filtration methods: the \(\varepsilon\)-lower-star filtration (ELSF), the \(L_p\) filtration (LpF), and the softmax filtration (SMF). {ELSF introduces a dimension-dependent delay to the maximum-vertex rule,} allowing higher-dimensional simplices to enter the filtration after their boundary faces, whereas {LpF and SMF use aggregation functions that depend on all vertex values rather} than solely on their maximum. By modifying how filtration values are assigned, these methods allow simplices to enter the filtration more progressively, so that topological features such as loops and voids may persist over longer filtration intervals rather than being filled immediately. Consequently, the resulting persistence diagrams may include persistence features that are not observed under LSF, potentially providing useful information for distinguishing data populations. Experimental results on simulated and real-world datasets demonstrate that the proposed filtration methods are computationally efficient and can provide greater sensitivity to structural differences in the data than LSF.
stat Machine Learning.comment: This is the published version of the article. Published in *International Journal of Topology*, MDPI, DOI: 10.3390/ijt3040025. Link to the official version: https://doi.org/10.3390/ijt3040025

stat Machine Learning.title: Simple Extensions of Single-Objective Acquisition Functions and Hedge Strategies for Multi-Objective Bayesian Optimization
stat Machine Learning.summary: Multi-objective Bayesian optimization (MOBO) is commonly approached through specialized acquisition functions or scalarization schemes designed to explicitly account for trade-offs among non-preferential objectives. In this work, we show that such complexity might be unnecessary. We propose a framework that extends standard single-objective acquisition functions directly to the multi-objective setting through a hypervolume-based methodology. We further extend hedge strategies for acquisition functions, which are typically used only in single-objective optimization, to the multi-objective regime. Our approach requires minimal modification to existing Bayesian optimization pipelines and avoids the need for bespoke multi-objective formulations. We demonstrate how a broad class of commonly used single-objective acquisition functions and hedge strategies can be adapted in a principled manner to handle multiple objectives, while preserving their intuitive interpretation and computational efficiency. Empirically, we evaluate the proposed methods across a range of synthetic and real-world multi-objective benchmarks. Despite their simplicity, our extensions consistently match or outperform more complex state-of-the-art MOBO methods in terms of optimization performance and sample efficiency. These results suggest that effective multi-objective Bayesian optimization can be achieved by reusing and carefully extending well-established single-objective acquisition strategies, offering a simpler and more flexible alternative to existing approaches.
stat Machine Learning.comment: 40th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2026)

stat Machine Learning.title: Identifying Drift, Diffusion, and Causal Structure from Temporal Snapshots
stat Machine Learning.summary: Stochastic differential equations (SDEs) are a fundamental tool for modelling dynamic processes, including gene regulatory networks (GRNs), contaminant transport, financial markets, and image generation. However, learning the underlying SDE from data is a challenging task, especially if individual trajectories are not observable. Motivated by burgeoning research in single-cell datasets, we present the first comprehensive approach for jointly identifying the drift and diffusion of an SDE from its temporal marginals. Assuming linear drift and additive diffusion, we show that non-identifiability can only arise if the initial distribution possesses generalized rotational symmetries. We further prove that even if this condition holds, the drift and diffusion can almost always be recovered from the marginals. Additionally, we show that the causal graph of any SDE with additive diffusion can be recovered from the identified SDE parameters. To complement this theory, we adapt entropy-regularized optimal transport to handle anisotropic diffusion and introduce APPEX (Alternating Projection Parameter Estimation from $X_0$), an iterative algorithm designed to estimate the drift, diffusion, and causal graph of an additive noise SDE, solely from temporal marginals, and demonstrate its effectiveness on simulated data from linear additive noise SDEs.

Computation.title: A Generalized Bayesian Approach to Clustering with Dimension Reduction
Computation.summary: Generalized Bayes product partition models provide a probabilistic counterpart to loss-based clustering. They update a prior over partitions through an exponentiated clustering loss rather than a likelihood, so allocation uncertainty can be quantified without a full generative model for the data. However, their performance depends on the space in which the loss is evaluated. For high-dimensional observations, a squared Euclidean loss on the raw features can be dominated by irrelevant coordinates or fail to reflect cluster structure lying near a nonlinear low-dimensional manifold. We propose an extension in which an autoencoder and the partition are learned together, so that the space in which the clustering loss is evaluated is shaped by the clustering itself. Our generalized posterior combines a reconstruction loss, which keeps the low-dimensional representation faithful to the observed data, with a within-cluster sum of squares in the latent representation, which encourages cluster separation. Posterior computation alternates between Gibbs sampling over partitions and gradient-based updates of the autoencoder network, with the learning rate estimated jointly. We illustrate the approach through simulation studies and applications to four benchmark datasets.

Computation.title: Sparse Probabilistic Richardson Extrapolation
Computation.summary: Almost every numerical task can be cast as extrapolation with respect to the fidelity or tolerance parameters of a consistent numerical method. This perspective enables probabilistic uncertainty quantification and optimal experimental design functionality to be deployed, and also unlocks the potential for the convergence of numerical methods to be accelerated. Recent work established Probabilistic Richardson Extrapolation as a proof-of-concept, demonstrating how parallel multi-fidelity simulation can be used to accelerate simulation from a whole-heart model. However, the number of simulations was required to increase super-exponentially in $d$, the number of tolerance parameters appearing in the numerical method. This paper develops a refined notion of 'extrapolation dimension', drastically reducing this simulation requirement when multiple tolerance parameters feature in the numerical method. Sparsity-exploiting methodology is developed that is simultaneously simpler and more powerful compared to earlier work, and this is accompanied by sharp theoretical guarantees and substantial empirical support.

Computation.title: Locally Adaptive Conformal Prediction for Polynomial Chaos Expansions
Computation.summary: This work develops a locally adaptive jackknife+ conformal prediction framework for polynomial chaos expansions. Therein, the non-conformity scores are normalized with an auxiliary polynomial chaos expansion trained on the log-transformed leave-one-out residuals of the base model. We show that the coverage guarantee of jackknife+ conformal prediction carries over to the adaptive intervals if the leave-one-out auxiliary models are trained on nested leave-one-out residuals. For fixed-basis polynomial chaos expansions fitted by ordinary least squares, all required quantities are derived in closed form and the guarantee-preserving adaptive intervals are obtained from a single model fit, without any model retraining. For sparse polynomial chaos expansions, where multiple model fits are necessary, we propose a heuristic simplification that limits the computational overhead of adaptivity at the cost of the formal coverage guarantee. Numerical experiments on an academic benchmark with known heteroscedastic noise and on an engineering simulation dataset show that the suggested method attains the target coverage while providing intervals that adapt to local prediction uncertainty, therefore being considerably more statistically efficient. These advantages are particularly prominent in high-uncertainty regions of the input space, where the performance of non-adaptive methods degrades substantially.

Computation.title: Circular interval-valued regression with application to wind direction: A cylindrical approach
Computation.summary: Many real-world datasets are inherently interval-valued, yet standard statistical methods are typically designed for point observations. Furthermore, intervals that are circular in nature may naturally exist. In this paper, we introduce a cylindrical regression framework for interval-valued circular data, addressing the joint challenges of the periodical nature and measurement uncertainty within the observed circular intervals. The proposed model accommodates a circular interval-valued response variable and both circular and linear covariates using a centre-range approach. To estimate the model, a maximum likelihood approach is proposed. The performance of the proposed estimation procedure is demonstrated through a simulation study. Application to two real-world datasets from a wind farm in South Africa and a weather station in Brazil further substantiates the model's practical value.

Computation.title: Coherent forecast combination for linearly constrained multiple time series
Computation.summary: Forecasting linearly constrained multiple time series, as those arising in National Accounts, energy systems and supply chain planning, requires that the forecasts of all variables jointly satisfy the underlying accounting or resource-balance identities. When several experts provide forecasts for some or all of the variables, classical forecast combination operates on each variable and ignores the linear constraints, while forecast reconciliation enforces such constraints by using a single forecast per variable. To bridge this gap, we develop an original coherent forecast combination framework, in which the joint problem of combination across experts and coherence across variables is formulated as a linearly constrained optimization problem. Closed-form expressions are derived for the coherent combined forecast and its error covariance matrix, and the statistical properties of the resulting estimators are discussed. A Monte Carlo experiment and a forecasting application to an Australian daily electricity generation dataset confirm that the proposed approach significantly improves forecast accuracy with respect to standard forecast combination and reconciliation alternatives.

Computation.title: New optimisations for exact, scalable 2D Gaussian process inference, with applications to astronomical time-series
Computation.summary:
Astronomical datasets often consist of a grid of datapoints in two or more dimensions, such as images, spectroscopic time-series, and imaging time-series. Gaussian processes (GPs) are a powerful tool for dealing with correlated noise in these data, arising from both astrophysical and instrumental systematics. Despite this, popular GP optimisations such as celerite are largely restricted to 1D datasets. Extensions to 2D data typically come with limited flexibility or poor scaling. As a motivating example, this limitation is significant for transiting exoplanet spectroscopy with JWST, as current analyses typically assume each spectroscopic light curve is statistically independent, despite many potential sources of wavelength-correlation, including detector readout noise and stellar granulation. This introduces a potential bias in atmospheric retrievals which is typically ignored.
  To solve this problem, we present new, exact GP optimisations implemented in the JAX-based package luas, which extend 1D GP optimisations to multidimensional data using Kronecker product algebra. These GP optimisations are highly flexible, permit efficient analysis of 2D datasets containing millions of datapoints, and in many cases have a cheaper cost than transit light curve modelling. These optimisations are key to pushing the limits of exoplanet spectroscopy to smaller targets around bright host stars, as we increasingly hit instrumental and astrophysical noise floors. We suggest further applications to the analysis of ground-based high resolution spectroscopic time-series, extreme precision radial velocities, and high-contrast imaging, drawing on the connection that certain 2D GP models represent a probabilistic generalisation of PCA. Applications may even extend to machine learning and geostatistics, as we present novel optimisations for the Linear Mixing Model and the Linear Model of Coregionalisation.

Computation.title: Hypergraph Generation via Structured Stochastic Diffusion
Computation.summary: Hypergraphs model higher-order interactions, but realistic hypergraph generation remains difficult because incidence, hyperedge-size heterogeneity, and overlap structure are not faithfully captured by pairwise reductions. We propose \HEDGE, a generative model defined directly on relaxed incidence matrices via a structured stochastic diffusion. The forward process combines a hypergraph-specific two-sided heat operator with an Ornstein--Uhlenbeck component, preserving structure-aware noising near the data while yielding an explicit Gaussian terminal law. Conditional on an observed hypergraph, this forward process is linear-Gaussian, so conditional means, covariances, scores, and reverse-drift targets are available in closed form. We therefore learn a permutation-equivariant state-only reverse-drift field in incidence space by regressing onto exact conditional targets, and generate samples by simulating a learned reverse-time SDE from the Gaussian base law. We establish exactness in the ideal state-only setting together with finite-horizon stability guarantees, and empirically show improved hypergraph generation quality relative to strong baselines.

Computation.title: Advection-aligned block Vecchia inference for spatio-temporal Gaussian processes
Computation.summary: Vecchia approximations enable scalable likelihood-based inference for large Gaussian process models, but their accuracy depends on the choice of conditioning sets. For spatio-temporal processes with advection, target-centered conditioning can omit informative past observations. Motivated by total column ozone observations from the Geostationary Environment Monitoring Spectrometer (GEMS), we propose a data-driven, advection-aligned block Vecchia approximation that incorporates estimated transport direction into temporal conditioning geometry. Observation locations need not lie on a regular grid. An initial advection vector is estimated from the data and used once to select transport-aligned past-time conditioning blocks. The resulting graph is held fixed during optimization, while covariance and advection parameters remain free to vary. This separates neighbor selection from covariance estimation, avoids repeated parameter-dependent neighbor searches, and provides an interpretable connection between conditioning geometry and estimated transport. Batched graphics processing unit (GPU) operations evaluate the likelihood and its gradients. In a matched comparison of daily GEMS datasets from July 2024 and July 2025, advection-aligned conditioning attained a lower fitted Vecchia negative log-likelihood than target-centered conditioning on 53 of 61 days. In six Matérn simulation scenarios with 120 matched eight-hour fields each, advection-aligned conditioning reduced advection-vector root mean squared error relative to target-centered conditioning at the same conditioning-block budget, with the largest reduction under strong transport.

Computation.title: An Exact Marginal Likelihood for Inference under Careless Responding
Computation.summary: Careless or insufficient-effort responding threatens the validity of self-report measurement. Mixture models for careless responding specify its form, and screening rules and robust methods depend on a threshold or tuning constant with no direct meaning in terms of careless responses. We propose ExHuber, a Bayesian method for inference on the engaged population under Huber's contamination model, in which an unknown proportion of responses comes from a contaminating distribution of unspecified form instead of the structural model. With a finite support of responses, such as the values of a scale score, a Dirichlet prior and a Beta prior on the contaminating distribution and its proportion yield a closed-form exact marginal likelihood of the structural parameters. Under a prior favoring a contaminating distribution on a few values, we show that the posterior of the structural parameters is consistent when careless responses occupy few values of the support, without knowing which values. Dynamic programming evaluates the marginal likelihood and its gradient at a cost quadratic in the sample size, which enables gradient-based sampling. Simulations from graded response models show accurate inference under straightlining and repeated response patterns, and an application to Big Five scales estimates the engaged mean of each scale.

Computation and Language.title: Multimodal Model Diffing for Feature Discovery and Control
Computation and Language.summary: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) exhibit strong visual understanding, yet the internal features that cause these behaviors remain difficult to identify, audit, or control. While applicable to post-hoc inspection, hidden states that are decomposed into interpretable feature directions using sparse autoencoders (SAEs) neither readily isolate which features are changed by multimodal training, nor are they directly useful for targeted control. We introduce MMDiff, a multimodal model-diffing framework that trains multimodal SAEs and turns them into feature-level interfaces for discovering and controlling multimodal behavior.
